summary.text: Brad Little is the incumbent Republican governor of Idaho, seeking a third term. A rancher by background, he served as a state senator and lieutenant governor before being elected governor in 2018 and re-elected in 2022.
As governor he signed the 2025 Idaho parental choice tax credit, a Medicaid cost-containment law that he said does not reject the voters' Medicaid expansion, and a 2022 income-tax cut.

paragraphs.text: Little was born and raised in Emmett, Idaho, on his family's sheep and cattle ranching operation.
He graduated from the University of Idaho in 1977 with a Bachelor of Science in agribusiness and ran the family's ranching operation.
Governor Dirk Kempthorne appointed Little to fill a state Senate vacancy in 2001, and he served in the Senate until 2009.
Gov. Butch Otter appointed him lieutenant governor in 2009, and he held that office until 2019.
Little won a crowded Republican primary and was elected governor in 2018, taking office on January 7, 2019.
He was re-elected in 2022, defeating Democrat Stephen Heidt and independent Ammon Bundy.
He married Teresa Soulen in 1978, and they have two sons.
